summary.text: A 17-year-old non-diabetic female who took metformin for PCOS was brought to the emergency department after ingesting approximately 30 tablets of metformin 500 mg in a suicidal attempt. On arrival she was fully conscious, oriented and hemodynamically stable with normal initial vital signs and a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15/15, and she reported nausea, abdominal pain and two episodes of vomiting.

Initial laboratory investigations at 14:00 hours showed normal serum electrolytes and normal kidney and liver function tests, a complete blood count was also reported, and plasma glucose was normal at 5.2 mmol/L. An arterial blood gas showed high anion gap metabolic acidosis with an anion gap of 14.1, pH 7.3 and lactate 5.7 mmol/L, and she was admitted to the intensive care unit for close monitoring.

During the first few hours of admission her blood pressure fell to 85/50 mmHg, requiring noradrenaline infusion and intravenous fluids, and she was sedated for increasing agitation and given intravenous sodium bicarbonate. Acidosis nevertheless worsened, with pH down to 7.1 and lactate peaking at 18 mmol/L; with a decreased level of consciousness, urgent intermittent hemodialysis was started and continued until the lactate target below 4 mmol/L was obtained after eight continuous hours.

Her clinical condition and mental status improved before the end of the dialysis session, and noradrenaline was tapered and discontinued after hemodialysis. The authors report repeated biochemistry the day after within the normal range, and she left the hospital after a few days in excellent clinical condition.
